newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN DOLLAR FIRM, BONDS SLIP ON JOBS DATA.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN DOLLAR FIRM, BONDS SLIP ON JOBS DATA.

text.p: The Australian dollar firmed and bonds eased after the July employment report came in much in line with analysts' expectations.

Employment rose by 21,300 compared with median expecations for a 25,000 increase, although it did include a 52,500 in full-time employment. the unemployment rate was 8.7 percent against an expected 8.6 percent.
The dollar was quoted at US$0.7355/60 compared with US$0.7340/45 just before the data release.
The September 10-year bond futures contract was 93.510 against a pre-data 93.540. September bill futures also eased, moving to 95.08 from 95.10
